Plotting results

Source: vignettes/plotting.Rmd
plotting.Rmd

The plot functions take the result of sdid() and return ggplot objects, which draw when printed and can be extended with +. They require ggplot2, and sdid_units_plot() uses ggrepel, when it is installed, to keep its labels apart.

library(sdid)
data(california_prop99)
fit = sdid(california_prop99, "PacksPerCapita", "State", "Year", "treated",
           vce = "placebo", seed = 1213, graph = FALSE, quietly = TRUE)

Trends

sdid_plot(), which plot() calls, draws the treated units’ average and the synthetic control. The red dashed line marks the start of treatment, midway between the last period before it and the first treated period. The gray band at the bottom shows the time weights, with their scale on the right-hand axis.

sdid_plot(fit)

The two lines may sit apart before treatment. Synthetic difference-in-differences asks the synthetic control to move in parallel with the treated units over the weighted pre-treatment periods, not to match their level.

style = "effects" adds a diagram of the comparison behind the estimate, with an arrow marking the effect.

sdid_plot(fit, style = "effects")

Individual units

spaghetti.units adds the trajectories of chosen units, here the three controls with the largest weights.

w = weights(fit)$omega
top = w$unit[order(-w$`1989`)][1:3]
sdid_plot(fit, spaghetti.units = top, spaghetti.label.size = 3)

spaghetti.matrices adds any other trajectories, given as a list with one matrix per estimate, each row a trajectory with a column per period and a row name that labels it. Here, the unweighted average of all controls, the comparison plain difference-in-differences makes.

Y = fit$setup$Y
average = rbind("Average of controls" = colMeans(Y[w$unit, , drop = FALSE]))
sdid_plot(fit, spaghetti.matrices = list(average), spaghetti.label.size = 3)

Comparing estimators

A named list of results draws each in its own panel, stacked and labeled by its name.

estimates = lapply(c(SDID = "sdid", SC = "sc", DID = "did"), function(m) {
  sdid(california_prop99, "PacksPerCapita", "State", "Year", "treated",
       method = m, vce = "noinference", graph = FALSE, quietly = TRUE)
})
sdid_plot(estimates)

Synthetic control puts no weight on the periods before treatment, so its panel has no band, and difference-in-differences weighs them equally. Each band is drawn on its own scale. lambda.comparable = TRUE draws them on a common scale instead, where a weight of 1 fills the band, so that their heights can be compared across panels.

Ticks

Each axis has about five nice ticks covering the data, as the Stata command chooses them, and a time axis of years gets ticks only at whole years. x.breaks and y.breaks set the ticks, which the axis range, frame and band follow. Adding a scale to the returned plot instead replaces the one it sets.

sdid_plot(fit, x.breaks = seq(1970, 2000, by = 5))

Unit weights

sdid_units_plot() shows each control’s own estimate, the difference-in-differences of the treated units with that control alone, whose average with the unit weights is the estimate. The default scatter plots each control’s weight against its own estimate, with controls given no weight drawn as open circles.

sdid_units_plot(fit)

The heavily weighted controls are at the right. Their spread about the red line shows whether they agree, and the open circles show whether the weighting changed the answer. type = "bars" draws the weighted controls from the largest weight down, each bar running from the estimate to the control’s own estimate, with its weight at the end.

sdid_units_plot(fit, type = "bars")

label.units names every control, those with weight, or the n with the largest weights. For a staggered result, each cohort gets a panel, with ten names each, unless cohort chooses one.

Placebo tests

sdid_placebo_plot() draws the estimate above an in-time placebo, which pretends treatment began earlier, at placebo.time, using only the periods before the real treatment. Where nothing happened, the placebo’s lines should keep tracking each other after its red line.

sdid_placebo_plot(fit, placebo.time = 1981)

sdid_placebo() returns the placebo estimate itself.

sdid_placebo(fit, placebo.time = 1981)
#> Synthetic difference-in-differences estimate -1.66742. Effective controls 15.9 of 38 and effective periods before treatment 1.0 of 11, with 1 treated unit and 8 periods after treatment.
